hint.p: If differentiating the entire equation all at once is too much to keep track of, try differentiating the left and right sides separately.

solution.p: Differentiating the right side is straightfoward, and gives \frac{d}{dx} (10x + 4y) = 10+4 \frac{dy}{dx}
Equating the two sides gives e^{x^2 y} \left({2x} + x^2 \frac{dy}{dx}\right) = 10+4 \frac{dy}{dx}
